From 7bca405c986075c99b9f729d3587b5c45db39d01 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Lucas Stach <l.stach@pengutronix.de>
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2024 19:50:26 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] bus: imx-weim: fix valid range check

When the range parsing was open-coded the number of u32 entries to
parse had to be a multiple of 4 and the driver checks this. With
the range parsing converted to the range parser the counting changes
from individual u32 entries to a complete range, so the check must
not reject counts not divisible by 4.

Fixes: 2a88e4792c6d ("bus: imx-weim: Remove open coded "ranges" parsing")
Signed-off-by: Lucas Stach <l.stach@pengutronix.de>
Signed-off-by: Shawn Guo <shawnguo@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/bus/imx-weim.c b/drivers/bus/imx-weim.c
index 6b5da73c8541..837bf9d51c6e 100644
--- a/drivers/bus/imx-weim.c
+++ b/drivers/bus/imx-weim.c
@@ -120,7 +120,7 @@ static int imx_weim_gpr_setup(struct platform_device *pdev)
 		i++;
 	}
 
-	if (i == 0 || i % 4)
+	if (i == 0)
 		goto err;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(gprvals); i++) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/bus/imx-weim.c`**
- The condition that checks the count of parsed entries has been modified. 
- The original check `if (i == 0 || i % 4)` has been changed to `if (i == 0)`. 
- This change removes the requirement that the count of entries (`i`) must be a multiple of 4, allowing for more flexible range parsing.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (identified by the hash `2a88e4792c6d`) that converted the range parsing from an open-coded method to a range parser. 
- The original implementation enforced a strict check on the number of entries, which was necessary for the open-coded parsing but became unnecessary with the new range parser. 
- The patch ensures that the driver no longer rejects valid counts that are not divisible by 4, thus fixing the issue related to range parsing.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
for_each_of_range(&parser, &range) {
    ...
    i++;
}
```
```c
if (i == 0 || i % 4)
```
Reason:
The original implementation required the count of entries (`i`) to be a multiple of 4, which was enforced by the condition `i % 4`. However, with the transition to the range parser, this requirement was no longer valid, leading to incorrect validation of valid entry counts when the number of entries was not divisible by 4.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (i == 0)
```
Reason:
The fix removes the check for `i % 4`, allowing the function to accept any valid count of entries, as the new range parser does not impose the restriction that the count must be a multiple of 4. This change ensures that valid configurations are not incorrectly rejected.
